title: Dedicated escape-hatch: regional throttle playbook and tenant preemption policy
creator: Maya Ortega
description: Design and implement an "escape-hatch" suite for Dedicated/Private control planes to: (1) keep latency and availability SLOs during partial infra failures and rolling upgrades, (2) provide per-region graceful failover, and (3) safely preempt or degrade noisy tenants via circuit-breaker + staged load-shedding. This ticket covers the playbook, admission-controller changes, canary upgrade steps, and a prototype operator for automated emergency throttles.
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane admission controller exposes per-tenant and per-region circuit-breaker metrics and break/recover endpoints
Automated regional tilt strategy that shifts traffic from failing region to standby region with 3-step canary (10%/50%/100%) and health checks
Load-shedding policy engine supports priority bands (reserved, best-effort) and can preempt best-effort requests when node CPU > 70% for >2m
Rolling upgrade runbook updated: drain, 10m cooldown, tenant-aware eviction, and automatic rollback trigger on p95 latency regression >15%
Runbook tested in staging by executing simulated region outage and noisy-tenant scenario with measurable SLO adherence

decision_log: Use two-tier fuse behavior: soft-fuse (automated partial shedding + circuit-breaker backoff) and hard-fuse (full tenant quarantine) — soft first to avoid customer-visible hard drops.
Region failover will be rate-limited and health-checked (10% → 50% → 100% weight shift over 10 minutes) instead of instant DNS swap to avoid downstream capacity spikes.
Preemption order: best-effort tenants -> burst tenants -> reserved tenants. Reserved tenants are only preempted when >95th percentile node exhaustion persists >5m and no alternative region capacity.
Rolling upgrades will include tenant-aware draining: evict best-effort pods first and keep reserved capacity pinned until final stages of the rollout.

We will not rely on immediate synchronous KV cache replication for failover; instead use a read-through cache with cold-warm warming in the target region and accept temporary latency increase during failover.

notes_for_oncall: If p95 control-plane latency > 1.15x baseline after a rollout, flip feature flag off: /admin/features/dedicated-escape-hatch = false
To manually quarantine a tenant: POST /admin/fuse/:tenant hard (requires 2FA & Ops approval). Use only for proven noisy tenants impacting reserved classes.
Emergency region failover: follow runbook section 'regional-tilt' — move 10% traffic and monitor healthy_upstream_requests and model_kv_warmup_progress before next weight step.
If automated soft-fuse triggered unexpectedly, gather logs: admission_controller.log, kubelet metrics, tenant-request-queue metrics and open an incident ticket referencing ENG-50123.
